ARCH=HEX,DI,DIP,NO_CROSS_LAYER,PORT_FLOW_OUT_IN,DOTENV_WALKUP,LAYOUT_LAYOUT,NO_LAYER_ROOT_FILES,ENV_ADAPTER,SEVERITY
ARCH.HEX=Hexagonal. domain innermost, application owns ports, infrastructure provides adapters, control wires and starts.
ARCH.DI=All dependencies constructed in control/dependencyInjection/AppContainer and passed in. No service locators, no globals.
ARCH.DIP=Port traits live in application/ports. Adapters in infrastructure/<port-folder>/ implement them. Domain imports nothing from application or infrastructure.
ARCH.NO_CROSS_LAYER=Each layer depends only on the layer directly below it. domain <- application <- infrastructure <- control.
ARCH.PORT_FLOW_OUT_IN=Outbound port defined in application/ports, inbound adapter in infrastructure/<port-folder>/.
ARCH.DOTENV_WALKUP=MANDATORY. Walk up from the application root toward the filesystem root, first .env hit loads, none found yields an empty DotEnv. System environment variables override .env values. ${VAR} expands inside values, depth limit 10, circular and self references are a hard error. Unquoted and double-quoted values expand; single-quoted values are literal.
ARCH.LAYOUT_LAYOUT=application divides into services, ports, useCases and nothing else. infrastructure divides into one folder per application port plus the Env adapter. domain contains models and valueObjects only. control divides into dependencyInjection and entryPoint.
ARCH.NO_LAYER_ROOT_FILES=HARD_FAIL. No source file sits directly in a layer root; every file lives in a nested folder.
ARCH.ENV_ADAPTER=infrastructure/env is the Env adapter. Env.load resolves configuration. After this feature it consults the process environment first, then the discovered .env, then application.conf.
ARCH.SEVERITY=Every CU in this ITR is implicitly SEVERITY:CRITICAL. A stub, a missing feature, or a DIP violation is a hard fail. Report and stop.
ARCH.SCALA=This is Scala 3.3.4. Significant indentation syntax, no braces for blocks. Match the surrounding file style exactly.
ARCH.STANDALONE=bugfix-feature-5 criterion 4 stands: the two pipeline trees reference only their own files. No shared module. Code duplicated across trees is correct, not a defect.
ARCH.BRONZE_IS_RAW=Bronze lands what arrives, unfiltered. Do not reject, coerce, normalise or drop enrichment values at the sink. Filtering and vocabulary normalisation are silver-layer concerns and are out of scope for every CU here.
ARCH.OUT_OF_SCOPE=Silver, gold, deduplication, taxonomy and the launcher executable are not addressed by any CU in this ITR.

LEGEND.SCALA_SIG=Significant-indentation Scala 3. A method body is introduced by `:` and indented; `do` introduces loops; `then` introduces conditionals.
LEGEND.OPAQUE_TYPE=An opaque type alias over a primitive. `opaque type GeoArea = String` gives a distinct static type but permits any String. It is NOT a closed vocabulary.
LEGEND.SEALED_TRAIT=A closed algebraic type. The permitted inhabitants are exactly the case objects or case classes listed. No other value can be constructed, which is how a controlled vocabulary is enforced at compile time.
LEGEND.EITHER=Sum type. Left is the failure, Right the success. Preferred over exceptions for expected failures per ARCH.PYTHON.MONADIC_ERROR, applied here by analogy since the codebase is Scala.
LEGEND.PROVE_LINE=A `Prove: ` backtick-quoted shell command that proves the preceding step succeeded. Every numbered step carries one.
LEGEND.DO_NOT_TOUCH=A closed list of paths the Coder must not modify. Violation is a MAJOR architecture deviation.
LEGEND.STOP_WHEN=The condition under which the Coder halts and reports rather than continuing.
LEGEND.MIRROR_CU=A CU whose deliverable is a byte-identical copy of another CU's file into the sibling pipeline tree, required by ARCH.STANDALONE.
LEGEND.CRITERION_REF=An ARCH.DOTENV clause or numbered acceptance criterion from the feat-8 specification.
LEGEND.S3A=Hadoop's S3 filesystem. Spark resolves an s3a:// URI through it. Without hadoop-aws on the classpath and fs.s3a.* settings supplied, s3a:// falls back to the public AWS endpoint.
LEGEND.PATH_STYLE=Address form where the bucket is a path segment (http://host:port/bucket/key) rather than a DNS subdomain. Required for single-host S3-compatible stores; localhost cannot serve virtual-host-style names.
LEGEND.CU_ID=Zero-padded three-digit identifier, cu-001 through cu-010.
LEGEND.WAVE=An ordered group of CUs that may run in parallel because they touch disjoint files.

REQUIREMENTS:
Stop the readiness gate from reporting a healthy object store as missing.

The probe sets `Authorization: Bearer <accessKey>:<secretKey>`. S3 has no Bearer scheme; it authenticates with SigV4. Measured against the RustFS instance on this host:

```
signed head-bucket, existing bucket      -> success
signed head-bucket, nonexistent bucket   -> error
unsigned HEAD /lakehouse                 -> 403
unsigned HEAD /no-such-bkt               -> 403
unsigned HEAD + fabricated Bearer header -> 400
GET /health                              -> 200
```

So the fabricated header turns a healthy bucket into 400, and the gate blocks startup while the object store is UP. Dropping the header and accepting 403 would ALSO be wrong: RustFS answers 403 for a bucket that does not exist, so that would report ready when the bucket is absent. Only a SigV4-signed request distinguishes the two, and this CU does not implement SigV4.

The probe therefore switches to `/health`, the store's own liveness endpoint, and drops the Authorization header entirely. The claim narrows honestly: it proves the store is live, not that the bucket exists. A missing bucket then surfaces at the first write, which reports it clearly. Criterion 10's promise that the gate verifies the bucket is explicitly withdrawn in the feature spec rather than silently unmet.

The unused accessKey and secretKey parameters are removed and the AppContainer call site updated in the same CU, so no dead parameters survive.

# IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:

1. Change `pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/bronze/ObjectStoreReadinessProbe.scala` to probe `/health` with no Authorization header, and drop the two credential parameters. Everything else in the class, including the name string and the guard order, is preserved.

```scala
package newspipe.infrastructure.bronze

import newspipe.application.ports.{ObjectStoreReadinessProbe, ProbeResult}

import java.net.{HttpURLConnection, URI}
import scala.util.Try

final class HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe(
    endpoint: String,
    bucket: String,
    timeoutMillis: Int
) extends ObjectStoreReadinessProbe:
  def name: String = "object-store"

  def check(): ProbeResult =
    if endpoint.isEmpty then ProbeResult.NotReady(name, "no endpoint configured")
    else if bucket.isEmpty then ProbeResult.NotReady(name, "no bucket configured")
    else
      val health: URI = URI.create(s"$endpoint/health")
      Try:
        val conn: HttpURLConnection = health.toURL.openConnection().asInstanceOf[HttpURLConnection]
        try
          conn.setRequestMethod("GET")
          conn.setConnectTimeout(timeoutMillis)
          conn.setReadTimeout(timeoutMillis)
          conn.connect()
          val code: Int = conn.getResponseCode
          conn.disconnect()
          code
        catch case e: Exception => throw e
      match
        case scala.util.Success(code) if code >= 200 && code < 400 => ProbeResult.Ready
        case scala.util.Success(code) => ProbeResult.NotReady(name, s"liveness probe at $endpoint/health returned HTTP $code")
        case scala.util.Failure(e) => ProbeResult.NotReady(name, s"cannot reach $endpoint: ${e.getMessage}")
```

   Prove: `grep -q 'health' pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/bronze/ObjectStoreReadinessProbe.scala && ! grep -q 'Authorization' pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/bronze/ObjectStoreReadinessProbe.scala && ! grep -q 'accessKey' pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/bronze/ObjectStoreReadinessProbe.scala && echo NO-AUTH-NO-DEAD-PARAMS`

2. Change `pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/dependencyInjection/AppContainer.scala` so the probe is constructed with three arguments. The surrounding readiness wiring, including the Kafka probe and the gate timings, is unchanged.

```scala

```

   Prove: `grep -c 'HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe(env.s3Endpoint, env.s3Bucket, 3000)' pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/dependencyInjection/AppContainer.scala`

3. Create `pipelines/ingestion/src/test/scala/newspipe/ObjectStoreReadinessProbeSpec.scala`. It drives a JDK HTTP server bound to an ephemeral port, so the suite needs no object store and no network, and it asserts the Authorization header is absent, which is the actual regression.

```scala
package newspipe

import newspipe.application.ports.ProbeResult
import newspipe.infrastructure.bronze.HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe
import org.scalatest.funspec.AnyFunSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers

import com.sun.net.httpserver.{HttpExchange, HttpHandler, HttpServer}

import java.net.InetSocketAddress

class ObjectStoreReadinessProbeSpec extends AnyFunSpec with Matchers:
  private var server: HttpServer = _
  private var lastAuth: String = null
  private var status: Int = 200

  private def start(): String =
    server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/health", new HttpHandler:
      def handle(ex: HttpExchange): Unit =
        lastAuth = ex.getRequestHeaders.getFirst("Authorization")
        val body: Array[Byte] = Array.emptyByteArray
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(status, body.length.toLong)
        ex.getResponseBody.write(body)
        ex.close()
    )
    server.start()
    s"http://127.0.0.1:${server.getAddress.getPort}"

  override def afterAll(): Unit = if server != null then server.stop(0)

  private def probe(endpoint: String): ProbeResult =
    new HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe(endpoint, "lakehouse", 2000).check()

  describe("HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe") {
    it("reports ready when the liveness endpoint answers 200") {
      status = 200
      probe(start()) shouldBe ProbeResult.Ready
    }
    it("sends no Authorization header at all") {
      status = 200
      probe(start())
      lastAuth shouldBe null
    }
    it("reports not-ready naming the endpoint when the liveness probe fails") {
      status = 503
      val result = probe(start())
      result match
        case ProbeResult.NotReady(dep, detail) =>
          dep shouldBe "object-store"
          detail should include("503")
        case other => fail(s"expected NotReady, got $other")
    }
    it("reports not-ready when the endpoint refuses the connection") {
      val result = probe("http://127.0.0.1:1")
      result shouldBe a[ProbeResult.NotReady]
    }
    it("reports not-ready when no endpoint is configured") {
      new HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe("", "lakehouse", 2000).check() shouldBe
        ProbeResult.NotReady("object-store", "no endpoint configured")
    }
    it("reports not-ready when no bucket is configured") {
      new HttpObjectStoreReadinessProbe("http://127.0.0.1:1", "", 2000).check() shouldBe
        ProbeResult.NotReady("object-store", "no bucket configured")
    }
  }

```

   Prove: `cd pipelines/ingestion && sbt "testOnly newspipe.ObjectStoreReadinessProbeSpec"`

4. Run the suite, then run the pipeline end to end against the live RustFS and Kafka. Step 4 is the reason this CU exists: the previous defect was invisible to every unit test, because both suites only ever exercised the negative path.

```sh
cd pipelines/ingestion && sbt test
```

   Prove: `cd pipelines/ingestion && sbt test | tail -5`

Do NOT touch: `pipelines/enrichment/**` (cu-016), `pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/**` (the discovery fix landed in wave 7), `pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/application/**` (the port vocabulary is correct and must not change), `pipelines/ingestion/build.sbt`, `conf/**`, `.LLMDD/**`.
Stop when the stated Prove command exits 0. On failure, record the failing case and the observed value in per-CU feedback rather than weakening an assertion.

ACCEPTANCE:
AC-1 The probe sends no Authorization header. This is the defect: a fabricated header is what produced the 400 against a healthy bucket.
AC-2 A store whose /health answers 200 yields ProbeResult.Ready.
AC-3 A store whose /health answers 5xx yields NotReady naming the endpoint and the status.
AC-4 An endpoint that refuses the connection yields NotReady rather than an exception escaping check().
AC-5 An empty endpoint or an empty bucket yields NotReady with the specific message, before any request is attempted.
AC-6 AppContainer constructs the probe with three arguments; `grep -c 'accessKey' ObjectStoreReadinessProbe.scala` prints 0.
AC-7 ARCH.PYTHON.NO_ANY analogue for Scala -- no null is returned and no exception escapes check(); every failure path returns a NotReady value.
AC-8 The specification drives a stub HTTP server, so it contacts no real object store and no network.
AC-9 END TO END, the point of this CU: with RustFS and Kafka up, `sbt run` from pipelines/ingestion gets past the gate and reaches the poll loop instead of exiting 1. A pre-fix run exits 1 with "startup aborted, not ready: object-store: bucket 'lakehouse' returned HTTP 400".
AC-10 The same run must not emit "HADOOP_HOME and hadoop.home.dir are unset" as a cause of failure. If it appears AND the poll loop does not start, report both verbatim in per-CU feedback rather than suppressing the message; that outcome means the warning is load-bearing and needs its own CU.
AC-11 `sbt test` exits 0 from pipelines/ingestion.
AC-12 ARCH.STANDALONE - `grep -rn 'pipelines/enrichment' pipelines/ingestion/` prints nothing.

Mirror cu-015 into the enrichment tree. The probe and its call site are byte-identical across trees, so both copies are file operations rather than re-derivations. The same end-to-end run applies, and it is more demanding here because enrichment additionally gates on the opencode binary.
